headword: {宝塚歌劇団|たからづかかげきだん}
reading: たからづかかげきだん

definitions.explanation: A musical theatre company based in Takarazuka, Hyōgo, in which women play all the roles, male and female. Founded in 1913 by the railway entrepreneur Kobayashi Ichizō, it gave its first performance in 1914.

notes:
Usually called simply {宝塚|たからづか}, or ヅカ among fans. Members train first at the {宝塚音楽学校|たからづかおんがくがっこう}, then join one of five troupes: {花組|はなぐみ}, {月組|つきぐみ}, {雪組|ゆきぐみ}, {星組|ほしぐみ} and {宙組|そらぐみ}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {男役|おとこやく}: a performer who plays male roles (the stars of the company)
- {娘役|むすめやく}: a performer who plays female roles
- タカラジェンヌ: a Takarazuka performer
- {宝塚|たからづか}⟦ファン→ファン：10065_fan⟧: a Takarazuka fan

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kobayashi founded the company to bring passengers to the hot-spring resort at the end of his railway line, which later became the Hankyu Railway. Its lavish revues and its devoted, mostly female audience are a well-known part of Japanese popular culture.
